about: Where the 12 painted texture sets made for AssaultG3 came from and how to make them again. regenerate.sh runs these commands in this order. Paths are relative to the texforge output folder (regenerate.sh: <out>/texforge/); every command is given as the arguments after `texforge --out <that folder>`.
prompts: All seven `texforge gen` prompts are exact (copied from the scripts that ran them). A new gen does not give the same pictures: the five tiles and the four leak and scrape decals will come out as new pictures of the same material, so choose the candidate by eye by "chosen_because". The three hand-made decals and the two soft variants (given the same chosen candidates) are reproduced exactly.

requires.texforge: a texforge with these gen / make / decal options; gen needs an image generator (texforge's default backend is the codex CLI; TEXFORGE_GENERATOR=command runs your own). A generator never gives the same picture twice: regenerated tiling sets differ from the originals
requires.python: numpy and Pillow for make_decals.py and soften.py (byte-identical with numpy 1.26.4, Pillow 10.4.0)
requires.fonts: arialbd.ttf (Arial Bold) and Inkfree.ttf (Ink Free), from a Windows Fonts folder, for make_decals.py to give the original pictures byte for byte; without them it draws with a free font it finds (Liberation Sans, DejaVu Sans), and the stencil's and the label's lettering differ a little

layout: _materials/<name>/: <name>_BaseColor.png, <name>_Height.png, <name>.texforge.json, and <name>_Opacity.png for a decal. Each record (.texforge.json) also carries params.source, the absolute path of the picture it was made from on the machine that made it; that path differs from machine to machine. For the seven decals it was checked to be the only difference in the record; the five tile records were not regenerated in the check.
used_on_frame: AssaultG3 weapons/assault_g3/weapon.py: tile sets through the named finishes (weaponforge/finish.py) per material kind; decal boxes in cm in the weapon frame (x toward the muzzle, +Y its left, +Z up), "from" the side the picture is laid on from
order: gen poly_mould, rubber, anodised, phosphate, turned, leak_src, scrape_src
decal label_14, stencil_07, witness, leak, scrape, leak_soft, scrape_soft

command: hard-anodised aluminium surface in a dark charcoal grey, a fine even bead-blasted matte grain, very faint straight parallel machining passes running horizontally, even
source.prompt: hard-anodised aluminium surface in a dark charcoal grey, a fine even bead-blasted matte grain, very faint straight parallel machining passes running horizontally, even
source.prompt_status: exact, word for word: copied from the generation script that was run, not recalled
source.template: texforge's material template (prompts.material_prompt) wraps the prompt
source.prompt_as_sent: A square, flat, top-down / straight-on texture swatch of hard-anodised aluminium surface in a dark charcoal grey, a fine even bead-blasted matte grain, very faint straight parallel machining passes running horizontally, even. Orthographic, perfectly straight-on view with absolutely no perspective and no camera tilt. Flat, even, diffuse lighting from everywhere: NO cast shadows, NO directional light, NO highlights, NO vignette, NO lens effects, NO depth of field, NO watermark, NO text, no borders or frame. The material fills the entire frame edge to edge. Physically plausible, photoreal PBR albedo-style photograph scan of the material with fine natural detail, sharp focus everywhere, high resolution. Keep colour variation natural but avoid any single dominant landmark, large stain or gradient (it will be tiled). Keep the pattern axis-aligned (horizontal courses / rows, vertical joints) if it has one.
source.prompt_as_sent_note: the prompt after texforge's CLI template: the text the CLI hands to gen.generate (the texforge copy used had not changed prompts.py or gen.py since before the pass). gen.generate puts it between <<<PROMPT / PROMPT>>> markers inside its own fixed instruction to the Codex agent (gen.py INSTRUCTION: use the built-in image tool, pass the prompt verbatim, one image). What the image model itself finally received was not recorded
source.chosen_because: src_1 has a visibly brighter left half; src_2 is even, with the horizontal passes

process.record: plaster type: min-cut seams, overlap 1/6, despeckle k=4; height depth 0.4 cm; normal from height, height from luminance (no Codex in make)

used_on.finish: finish.anodised_alloy (texture "anodised", laid at 2 cm, tone 0.10, relief 0.6)
used_on.where: the 'alloy' kind: the top cover and the rail (satin black hard-anodised alloy)

source.prompt_as_sent: A single dark brown-black oily grime streaks running straight down from a short horizontal line at the top: thin dirty drips of gun oil mixed with dust, narrow and dense at the top, thinning and fading out lower down, vertical drawn as an isolated surface decal on a perfectly plain, uniform, flat pure white background (no gradient, no texture, no shadows, no floor). Straight-on orthographic view, flat lighting, no perspective, no text, no border. The mark is centred and fully contained with generous empty margin all around it (nothing touches the image edge), its edges fade naturally and softly into the background. Photoreal, high resolution, physically plausible.
